theme: O LORD, you have searched me and known me
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 139:1-18. David marvels that God knows him completely. Notice how the psalm moves from knowing to presence to creation to wonder.
settingTheScene: Psalm 139 is one of the most personal psalms. David reflects on the fact that God knows everything about him, is present everywhere, and made him in the womb. The last verses (19 to 24) turn to a prayer against the wicked and a prayer to be searched, but today’s reading covers the first eighteen verses, the part that has comforted many. It follows the Psalm 36 theme of God’s vast care.
observation: “O LORD, you have searched me and known me!” (v. 1).
“You know when I sit down and when I rise up; you discern my thoughts from afar” (v. 2).
“Even before a word is on my tongue, behold, O LORD, you know it altogether” (v. 4).
“Where shall I go from your Spirit? Or where shall I flee from your presence?” (v. 7).
“For you formed my inward parts; you knitted me together in my mother’s womb” (v. 13).
“I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Wonderful are your works; my soul knows it very well” (v. 14).
“Your eyes saw my unformed substance; in your book were written, every one of them, the days that were formed for me, when as yet there was none of them” (v. 16).
“How precious to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is the sum of them!” (v. 17).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with complete knowledge. God has searched David and known him. He knows when David sits and stands, knows his thoughts from far off, and knows his words before he speaks them. He hems David in, behind and before, and lays his hand on him. David’s response: “Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high; I cannot attain it.”

This could feel threatening, to be known so completely. But for David it is a comfort. The question in verses 7 to 12 shows that he has considered escape and found that there is none. “Where shall I go from your Spirit?” If he goes up to heaven, God is there. If he makes his bed in Sheol, God is there. If he takes the wings of the morning and dwells in the uttermost parts of the sea, even there God’s hand will lead him. Even darkness is not dark to God. The presence of God, which could be terrifying for a sinner, is a source of safety for a child.

Then the psalm goes back before birth. God formed his inward parts and knitted him together in his mother’s womb. “I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” This is a deep affirmation of the value of every human being. Each of us is a work of God, planned and watched over from the beginning. In his book were written all the days that were formed for us, before any of them existed. Our lives are known to God and held by him.

And David’s response is awe: “How precious to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is the sum of them! If I would count them, they are more than the sand.” When I awake, he says, I am still with you.

In John, Jesus is shown to know people completely. He knows Nathanael under the fig tree and the Samaritan woman’s history. To be known by him is to be known by God, and to be loved.
connection: Jeremiah 1:5 says God knew the prophet before he formed him in the womb. Job 10:8-12 and Psalm 119:73 also speak of God’s making. Proverbs 15:3 says the eyes of the LORD are in every place. John 1:47-49 and 4:16-19 show Jesus knowing people. Hebrews 4:13 says no creature is hidden from his sight. Matthew 10:29-31 says the very hairs of your head are numbered. Ephesians 2:10 says we are his workmanship.
application:
Read verses 1 to 6 slowly, and let yourself be fully known. Is that comforting or uncomfortable? Tell God.

Thank God for how he made you, including the parts you struggle to accept.

Share Psalm 139:13-14 with someone who feels worthless.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he has searched you and knows you.
Tell him what you want him to see in you today.
Praise him that you are fearfully and wonderfully made.
